runners_data.name: Mobadir
runners_data.note: Hold-up style suits this pace setup ideally; Ed Walker's youngster has consistent placed form at 6f on good but is winless in three nursery tries — Kieran Shoemark holds a strong book and this represents a significant upgrade in tactics if the front-runners exhaust each other.|

runners_data.name: Dissenter
runners_data.note: Won on good and has run only twice, giving trainer Marcus Tregoning options; returning just 10 days after her last run suggests she is in form, and Ashley Lewis' claim helps at 129lbs — prominent style means she sits just off the duel in a useful position if she doesn't get dragged into it.|

runners_data.name: Harry's Pop
runners_data.note: Prominent racer whose form figures include 4ths and a wide variety of going types but no wins; Stevie Donohoe is a capable claimer but the trainer's 14-day strike rate of 2/25 gives limited confidence, and sim-going stats (0 wins from 1 relevant run) are uninspiring.|

runners_data.name: Leucothea
runners_data.note: One of the two confirmed pace-setters; Sean Levey is a high-quality rider who will manage the duel intelligently, but Leucothea's last run was an 18th at 5f on good and her OR of 71 suggests she is competitive — her placed form (2nd, 3rd) shows she can finish races when not maxed out early.|

runners_data.name: Star People
runners_data.note: The other confirmed leader and the primary pace rival to Leucothea; Marco Ghiani rides confidently and Star People has consistent placed form at 6f on good, including a recent second, but three runs without a win and a contested lead raises questions about whether she finishes the race out when pressure comes.|

runners_data.name: Boleto
runners_data.note: Highest-weighted runner at 135lbs carrying the burden of a top-rated 74 OR; Clive Cox's hold-up juvenile won on good going at 6f earlier this season but has slipped to a 6th since — Rossa Ryan is an elite rider who will have him settled and ready to deliver a late run if the pace scenario unfolds.|

runners_data.name: Fern Clyde
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's consistent filly has strong recent form — win plus three places from last five including 4th, 3rd, 1st, 3rd, 4th — and headgear (hood) is listed; Jake Dickson's 5lb claim helps offset 133lbs, and excellent sim-going stats (5 from 6 relevant runs on good, 1 win 3 placed) make her a leading player if she travels smoothly behind the duel.|

races.paceDynamic: Star People and Leucothea are both confirmed front-runners and will clash for the lead from the stalls on this flat Nottingham 6f, creating a genuinely contested early pace rather than a soft, uncontested gallop. Sean Levey on Leucothea and Marco Ghiani on Star People will both want to dictate, meaning the opening two furlongs should be run at an honest tempo that stretches the field early. Prominent racers Dissenter, Harry's Pop, and Fern Clyde will sit just off that duel and be dragged into a fast early rhythm, which historically on this straight Nottingham track suits horses who can travel smoothly in behind and pick up in the final two furlongs. The race shape — a genuine pace duel up front with prominent horses under pressure through the middle — most favours hold-up and late-finishing profiles like Boleto and Mobadir, who can conserve energy while the leaders empty each other out.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Duel, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Star People and Leucothea burn each other off at a contested tempo, leaving the race wide open from 2f out.
scenarios.body: The front two set an honest gallop that drains them in the final furlong, allowing horses held up behind the pace to swoop late down the straight. On good-to-firm Nottingham turf, the track rewards horses who travel with cover and produce a clean sustained finish rather than those who front-ran into the race.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Thrives
scenarios.trigger: If the pace duel is fierce enough to eliminate the leaders but one of the prominent stalkers times their run perfectly from just off the pace.
scenarios.body: A horse like Fern Clyde or Dissenter, tracking just behind the duelling front-runners at a controlled distance, avoids the worst of the early burn and has the stamina reserves to finish strongly. Dissenter's winning form on good going over this course and distance, combined with a light 10-day turnaround suggesting she's cherry-ripe, makes this credible.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If Leucothea or Star People gets an uncontested or softened lead after the other blinks and settles, conserving enough to kick clear.
scenarios.body: Should one of the duelling front-runners back off early, the survivor secures a comfortable position and the honest tempo becomes a measured one, enabling them to coast to the line on this flat track. Leucothea's placed form on soft and standard-to-fast going and Star People's recent second on good ground suggest either could be the beneficiary if the battle is brief.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Dead Heat Slow Burn
scenarios.trigger: If pace unexpectedly collapses — both front-runners over-race and fade, leaving a vacuum — and a prominent horse fills the gap rather than a hold-up horse.
scenarios.body: In a scrambled finish where the pace paradoxically implodes rather than burning steady, a prominent horse rather than a closer benefits from the chaotic rhythm. This is the least likely scenario given the likely natural contest between two genuine front-runners and the fast going.

watchPoints.text: Star People and Leucothea — monitor which of the two front-runners blinks first in the opening furlong; whichever capitulates early could drop dramatically while the survivor may have a live chance.

Boleto — Rossa Ryan's positioning in the first two furlongs is critical; if he is forced to race wider than ideal or gets caught in traffic behind the duelling pair, his late run could be compromised on this relatively tight flat track.

Fern Clyde's hood — headgear worn for the first time or re-applied can unpredictably sharpen or unsettle a juvenile; if she pulls hard behind the contested pace, it negates her stamina advantage in the final furlong.

Dissenter's short 10-day turnaround — watch her in the paddock for signs of freshness or sweatiness, as a two-run filly returning quickly can be surprisingly forward or alternatively slightly flat if the quick return catches up.

Going update at the track is reported as Good To Firm across all Nottingham races — significantly faster than the declared Good, which will advantage horses with proven fast-ground form and may catch out those whose best form came on softer surfaces like Leucothea (soft placed form) and Harry's Pop.

races.name: Weatherbysshop.co.uk Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Star Marian
runners_data.note: Loughnane's 3yo has won over 5f on Standard ground but holds only a 2-from-9 record on similar going, and her 59-day absence combined with racing outside her natural hold-up role makes her a significant each-way risk despite landing the mapped lead position.

runners_data.name: Up The Monk
runners_data.note: Appleby's 4yo has a poor record on Good ground (1 win from 15 runs, no places), and while the apprentice claim from Mason Paetel(5) offers some compensation, his true hold-up style compressed into midfield here robs him of whatever tactical advantage he might otherwise have.

runners_data.name: Little Jaybee
runners_data.note: Evans' 3yo carries the fade-in-finish flag that data has consistently flagged, and her form string of 9-8969 suggests she is deeply out of form; the visor is retained but has not yet sparked a revival, and 3-from-9 on similar going is the one thin positive.

runners_data.name: Sergeant Mayer
runners_data.note: Tinkler's 5yo has a solid record on Good ground (2 wins, 5 places from 11 runs) and is fresh enough after 16 days, but his natural closing style is compromised by the compressed midfield position he is likely to occupy in what shapes as a bunched sprint.

runners_data.name: Hurt You Never
runners_data.note: Adrian Nicholls' 7yo has raced exclusively on Good ground across his last 15 runs, logging 2 wins and 4 places — more course-relevant going form than any rival here — and the booking of claiming apprentice Jack Nicholls(3) keeps the weight manageable for a horse who has form to recommend him at this trip.

runners_data.name: Invincible Crown
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's 4yo boasts the sharpest recent 5f profile in the field — 1 win and 2 places from 7 runs on Good, including a win and a second in the last three starts — and while Tom Eaves cannot get him to his preferred hold-up berth in this shape, his raw form over course and going marks him as the standout profile horse.

races.paceDynamic: Star Marian is the lone mapped front runner in this 5f handicap, redistributed from her true hold-up role to the lead because no genuine pace-setter exists in the field — she is likely to find herself in front by default rather than design, setting a sustainable rather than punishing gallop on Good to Firm ground. Invincible Crown, Sergeant Mayer, and Up The Monk are all natural hold-up horses compressed into midfield on the map because the field cannot accommodate every off-pace type at the rear; in reality this race is likely to be run at a steady-to-moderate tempo with the whole field tracking in a tight bunch. Hurt You Never is the one runner who has demonstrated consistent course-and-distance form on similar going, logging all 15 recent runs on Good ground, and shapes as the most course-fit finisher in the race. The dominant pace shape here — a slowly-run sprint with a wall of hold-up horses unable to find their true position — strongly favours horses with raw finishing speed and the clearest form on this specific trip and going, rather than any strategic positional advantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steady Pace, Bunch Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Star Marian sets an uncontested, moderate gallop and the field arrives in a tight group at the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: With no genuine front runner pressing the tempo, the race crawls early and turns into a sprint from the two-furlong marker, suiting horses with pure finishing speed over 5f.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Pinches It
scenarios.trigger: If Star Marian, defaulting to the lead, finds herself travelling well and is never seriously challenged for the first three furlongs.
scenarios.body: A moderate gallop set in front on Good to Firm going can be enough for a class animal to steal the race, particularly if the hold-up horses behind are slow to organise.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Flier Gets Through
scenarios.trigger: If a slightly stronger-than-expected pace stretches the field and a hold-up horse finds a clear passage late.
scenarios.body: Invincible Crown has the best recent form at 5f on Good ground, including a win and a place from seven runs, and would benefit most if gaps open late.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the bunch races too tight for too long and the sprint home becomes a muddled, all-at-once scramble with no clear winner emerging early.
scenarios.body: A chaotic finish over 5f tends to produce a surprise result, and a lightly-weighted runner like Up The Monk — racing out of his natural hold-up role — could sneak a placing if he finds the rail.

watchPoints.text: Invincible Crown's last three runs show a win and two places over 5f on Good ground — if Tom Eaves can manoeuvre him into any kind of clear passage in the final furlong, his form profile makes him the most dangerous horse in the race.

Star Marian's natural hold-up style versus her mapped lead role is the key positional conflict to watch from the stalls — if she is reluctant to stride on and drifts back, the race loses its only nominal pace-setter and the tempo could become farcically slow.

Hurt You Never has the best going-specific record in the field but has not won in recent starts — watch whether Jack Nicholls(3) can get him balanced and travelling early, as a failed run here may reflect positional congestion rather than ability.

With five of six runners naturally wanting to race hold-up or midfield, the first furlong will determine everything — any horse that secures an early position on the fence could steal a march on rivals who are all jostling for the same ground simultaneously.

Sergeant Mayer's trainer Nigel Tinkler has hit a 3-from-30 strike rate over the past 14 days — active and placing horses, which is worth noting given Sergeant Mayer's underlying Good-ground record of 2 wins and 5 places from 11 starts.

races.name: Weatherbys BetTrends Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Dawn Of Liberation
runners_data.note: A veteran 7-year-old hold-up specialist trained by Ruth Carr with solid sim-going form (12 runs on Good, one win and six places), though 68 days since last run is a notable freshness query over 1m2f; apprentice Warren Fentiman's 3lb claim could be an asset if the race sets up for a strong late challenge.

runners_data.name: Sedeirah
runners_data.note: Edward Bethell's lightly-raced three-year-old showed two placings from three runs on Good ground and steps up to 1m2f for the first time, which is a real unknown, but the shorter turnaround of 16 days and Callum Rodriguez's booking from a trainer in strong recent form (5/28 T14) makes her interesting if the trip is within range.

runners_data.name: Del Corso
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's three-year-old has a win over 10f on Good and is progressing steadily; however, it is a natural hold-up type crowded out at the rear by the field's make-up and mapped to midfield, meaning Shoemark will need to find a way to race in a less natural role — the 0.93 style-fit flag is a genuine discount to its win prospects.

runners_data.name: Aussie Pearl
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's three-year-old is the race's only front-runner and will control the pace from the outset, wearing a hood for the first time (hg:p flagged) which may sharpen her early; she has not won in four starts but her four runs on Good/Soft show she handles varied ground, and dictating solo from the front makes her a realistic factor if the pace suits.

races.paceDynamic: Aussie Pearl is the sole confirmed front-runner in a four-runner field and will set off to lead from the gates, with no rival likely to challenge her for the position on early pace — she can dictate a comfortable, controlled tempo on the Good to Firm Nottingham surface over 1m2f. With three hold-up types behind her, the race will be run at whatever pace Aussie Pearl and Sean Bowen choose, and without pressure she can preserve energy through the straight before the closers make their moves late. Del Corso, Dawn Of Liberation, and Sedeirah all want to come from off the pace, meaning the challenge will arrive in one wave in the final two furlongs rather than through sustained pressure throughout. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses with a sharp late turn of foot, provided Aussie Pearl has not stolen enough ground at a slow tempo to make the margin unbridgeable — the tactical verdict is that late-finishing profiles are best suited, though a patient front-runner scenario is a live threat if the pace is slow enough to allow Aussie Pearl to control the race to the line.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Closers Swamp Lone Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Aussie Pearl sets a moderate gallop and the hold-up runners have enough fuel to close powerfully in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Aussie Pearl controls the race from the front at a sustainable but not-slow-enough clip, and the three closers launch together off the final bend; the horse with the sharpest acceleration in the straight wins. This shape suits Dawn Of Liberation and Sedeirah, who both show sim-going form on Good/Good to Firm and can deliver a sustained late run.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If Aussie Pearl dictates a deliberately slow tempo and the hold-up horses leave too much to do at the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: With no rival willing to go with her, Aussie Pearl slips the field from the front and builds an unassailable lead into the straight, using her freshness advantage after 39 days off. Jockey Sean Bowen, an accomplished judge of pace, would need to recognise the opportunity early and accelerate before the closers realise the danger.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Del Corso Defies Position
scenarios.trigger: If Del Corso, freed from covering ground at the rear by a slow pace, travels smoothly in mid-division and produces a strong finishing run.
scenarios.body: Ed Walker's progressive three-year-old has a win and two placings over 10f on Good ground and carries the benefit of a 16-day turnaround in form; Kieran Shoemark could push forward from his mapped midfield position to get closer to the pace than expected. However, the STYLE_FIT tag of 0.93 means Del Corso is racing out of role and must be discounted — its chance depends on conditions aligning perfectly.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Bunched Finish
scenarios.trigger: If a tactical, dawdling gallop produces a sprint finish with all four runners arriving together in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Aussie Pearl crawls in front, the closers bunch up on her heels with no clear daylight, and the race degenerates into a sprint from the two-furlong marker; in that scenario the horse freshest on its legs and fastest over a short distance benefits. This is the least likely shape in a small field with one established leader and three genuine hold-up types, and would require very unusual positional decisions from all jockeys.

watchPoints.text: Aussie Pearl's pace control is the pivotal variable — if Sean Bowen slips the field at the top of the straight and builds a lead of two or more lengths, the three hold-up types will have very little time to close on Good to Firm ground over 1m2f.

Sedeirah is stepping up significantly in distance from 8f to 10f for the first time; if she cannot sustain her run over the extra ground, the late finish scenario collapses to only Dawn Of Liberation as a reliable closer.

Del Corso's style-fit flag of 0.93 means Kieran Shoemark may attempt to push forward from midfield earlier than the horse's natural style dictates — watch for an uncharacteristic forward move leaving the back straight that could disrupt the pace map.

With only four runners, the race is unlikely to be truly end-to-end — jockeys may play a waiting game that compresses the field, meaning the quality of the final-furlong burst rather than stamina will be decisive.

Dawn Of Liberation's 68-day absence is worth monitoring in the market; Ruth Carr's 14-day strike rate of 4/23 suggests horses return fit, but any ring-rustiness from the gap would temper the hold-up runner's chance of producing a sharp enough late challenge.

races.name: Weatherbys Racing Bank Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Theme Park
runners_data.note: Six-year-old hold-up type with two wins and three places from 13 runs on similar going, bolstered by a four-day turnaround suggesting sharpness; the trip and conditions look tailor-made and Faye McManoman will be looking to produce a late challenge against an uncontested leader.

runners_data.name: Straight A
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who gets a dream scenario here with no rival to pressure them; Michael Appleby's 1/28 T14 strike rate tempers confidence and the horse's recent form (422544) shows consistency without dominance, but the free lead over a flat 1m½f on good-to-firm is a significant tactical asset.

runners_data.name: Symphony Of Joy
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse shifted to the midfield section of the map because the field is overloaded with rear-runners; Kevin & Lauren Frost's T14 strike rate is respectable but sim-going figures (4 from 7) are modest and the horse has no wins in the past five runs, limiting confidence even if the pace sets up for closers.

runners_data.name: G'Emmethegreenlite
runners_data.note: Returning after a 100-day absence for Seb Spencer, whose T14 record of 2/8 is workable; all recent runs have come at shorter distances (5-6f) so the step up to 1m½f is a significant unknown, though the good-to-firm going is familiar ground from all four sim-going runs.

runners_data.name: Venetian Lion
runners_data.note: William Haggas-trained three-year-old whose hold-up style has been mapped to midfield due to the density of rear-runners in this field; Tom Marquand is a strong booking but sim-going figures (2 from 4) and a recent sixth at 8f on similar turf suggest the horse is still finding its feet, with the step up in trip an open question.

runners_data.name: Pretty Spirited
runners_data.note: Showed real form when winning back-to-back on similar going at 8f, and though a 76-day absence and a subsequent defeat (12th on soft) cloud the picture, the return to good-to-firm is a clear positive; Tom Eaves partners a genuine hold-up type whose true position at the rear was redistributed to midfield on the map, and the trainer's 0/8 T14 run rate is a flag.

races.paceDynamic: Straight A is the lone confirmed front-runner in this six-runner field over 1m½f on good-to-firm ground at Nottingham, and with no rival willing or able to challenge for the lead, they will dictate a controlled, uncontested tempo from the outset. That sustainable gallop is unlikely to stretch the field early, meaning the race will compress into a procession before quickening in the home straight. Theme Park and G'Emmethegreenlite are genuine hold-up types who will track from off the pace, while Symphony Of Joy, Venetian Lion, and Pretty Spirited — all true hold-up horses — have been redistributed to midfield on the map purely because there are too many rear-runners for the shape to absorb; in practice, Straight A is almost certain to have the lead entirely to themselves. This race shape — a lone, uncontested leader setting a measured gallop — strongly favours genuine hold-up closers who have the late kick to reel in a front-runner who has not been pressured, with Theme Park, holding strong similar-going form, best positioned to exploit the setup.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Straight A Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Straight A bowls along in front at a comfortable pace with zero pressure, controlling the race from wire to turn.
scenarios.body: Straight A sets a measured tempo throughout, arriving at the straight in front with energy intact, forcing the field to chase and potentially finding just enough to hold on; a jockey on a controlled front-runner with no rival to push them can time the effort perfectly.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Storm Home Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely slow enough to compress the field and a finisher produces a decisive late burst.
scenarios.body: Straight A's uncontested lead becomes a double-edged sword — if the gallop is too steady, the hold-up horses meet them fresh and full of running in the final two furlongs; Theme Park's two recent wins at this trip and going profile make them the most dangerous closer in this setup.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Types Benefit
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is honest enough to soften the front-runner but not so strong that pure closers have the edge.
scenarios.body: Symphony Of Joy or Venetian Lion, tracking in the middle of the field, pick off a tiring Straight A without needing to make up maximum ground; both carry redistribution caveats and are not natural midfielders, so this scenario requires them to race more forwardly than their usual pattern.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Caught Cold
scenarios.trigger: If Straight A overcooks the pace or encounters interference, leaving the door open for a winner from an unconventional position.
scenarios.body: An unlikely scenario given the size of the field and the docile nature of the expected gallop, but a stumble or wide draw burn could see Straight A cooked turning in; G'Emmethegreenlite's fresh return after 100 days and unknown angle adds a small wildcard element.

watchPoints.text: Theme Park is the form horse on similar going with two recent wins at this trip — watch whether Faye McManoman times the challenge to arrive right at Straight A's quarters in the final furlong rather than too wide or too early.

Straight A's Mason Paetel (5lb claimer) must judge the pace precisely — if the gallop drifts too slow the hold-up horses will have too much energy in the tank, and too fast risks burning Straight A out before the straight.

G'Emmethegreenlite returns after 100 days having only raced at 5-6f previously — watch for any signs of greenness or trip trouble from Dale Swift as the distance is entirely uncharted territory for this three-year-old.

Pretty Spirited's trainer T14 figure of 0/8 is worth noting alongside the 76-day break — if the yard is not in form or the horse needed its first run back, expect it to be doing its best work late but without the sharpness to fully capitalise.

With five of six runners carrying hold-up or redistributed hold-up profiles, watch the sectionals entering the home straight — if Straight A has an eight-length lead at the turn, the closers simply will not get there on a flat, fast track.
